clue.text: Make two scores of forty

parts.note: cutting forty into two equal halves leaves a pair of twenties, and a score is twenty

explanation.surface: Someone running up a cricket total of forty in two neat twenties.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty, so halving forty gives two scores; the clue describes cutting something exactly in half.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut into two equal parts is the meaning, illustrated by halving forty into twenties.

clue.text: Garment person's given, with diamonds as accessory

parts.note: bod is informal British for a person
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone presented with diamonds as a fashion accessory.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting upper part of a dress is a piece of clothing.

clue.text: Note covering beat group in typical bar?

definitions.text: Note covering beat group in typical bar?

parts.words: Note covering beat group in typical bar?
parts.note: a musical note that lasts a full four beats fills a whole bar of common time

explanation.surface: A notice put up over a pop band playing in an ordinary pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat group' and 'bar' suggest a band in a pub, but they are the beats of a musical bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole note lasting four crotchets fills a bar of four-four, the most common time signature.

clue.text: Odd type of chain-mail found in waterway

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the following word are taken

explanation.surface: Peculiar armour discovered in a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd type of' seems to describe strange armour but takes the 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th and 9th letters of CHAINMAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial channel for boats or irrigation is a man-made watercourse.

clue.text: Has to overcome gravity on planet, methane type

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: Mars is the red planet

indicators.note: the word has wraps over and around the letter for gravity, overpowering it

parts.note: G is the standard symbol for gravity

explanation.surface: A gas on another world strong enough to defeat gravity, possibly methane.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means coming after, and 'to overcome' has the word wrap round the gravity symbol rather than defeat it.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is the chief component of the gas bubbling up from rotting vegetation in bogs and fens.

clue.text: A draw, going for promotion, carrying some weight

indicators.note: in a down clue going up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: to draw is to pull

explanation.surface: A team that drew still pushing for promotion while carrying extra weight.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'going for promotion' means reading upwards. All-up weight is the total weight of a loaded aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The total loaded weight of an aircraft, crew and cargo is its all-up weight.

clue.text: Not quite what's expected — just a little drop?

definitions.meaning: a deficit, the amount by which a total falls below what was hoped for
read literally, a brief tumble or small descent

explanation.surface: Results slightly below forecast, only a small dip.
explanation.definitionFit: A deficit is an amount below target, and a small drop is literally a brief tumble.

clue.text: Wanting the power to fly

parts.note: flying through the air without any engine, wanting meaning lacking power

explanation.surface: Someone longing for the ability to take to the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' looks like desiring but means lacking: flying with no engine power.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailplanes and birds with still wings move through the air without engine power.

clue.text: Foundered, with first of boats trapped here?

definitions.text: Foundered, with first of boats trapped here?

indicators.note: the word for foundered holds the other pieces caught inside it

parts.note: foundered means sank
with means and

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A ship went down with the leading boat stuck fast on a hazard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped' does double duty in the surface as boats stuck aground, which is why the whole clue also works as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge of sand under shallow water is where vessels founder and get stuck.

clue.text: Get very excited, finding path at last, to enter gorge

indicators.note: the letter goes into the word for gorge

parts.note: to gorge is to overeat

indicators.note: the last letter of the word path is taken

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to finally find a path into a ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gorge' suggests a ravine but is the verb to stuff oneself; 'at last' gives H and 'to enter' puts it inside OVEREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To become overexcited or agitated, figuratively as an engine running too hot.

clue.text: Cheap literature? Loved mine to be kinky!

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the two words are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A cheap paperback promising that a lover's tastes run to the kinky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be kinky' rearranges the letters of LOVED MINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheap popular paperback novel of melodrama or adventure, originally sold in America for ten cents.

clue.text: Some stars love laid-back style of French café

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: laid back means lying backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: café noir is French black coffee, so noir is a style of serving café

explanation.surface: Someone who loves the relaxed atmosphere of a French café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid-back' looks like a description of the café's mood but reverses NOIR to RION.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hunter is a prominent constellation, so it is a group of several stars.

clue.text: At last, I set to work, finally clearing rubbish

definitions.text: At last, I set to work

indicators.note: clearing away the final letter of the word for rubbish

parts.note: cobblers is British slang for nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone at last getting down to work and clearing out rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic first-person speech: a shoemaker works on a last, the foot-shaped block. 'finally clearing' removes the last letter, S.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoemaker repairs shoes on a last, the foot-shaped block, so he does his job at a last.

clue.text: Starts to prepare broth with different ingredient — this?

indicators.note: with here means holding, the two initials enclosing the other piece
the starts of the two following words give their opening letters

parts.note: different means other

explanation.surface: A cook beginning a broth but swapping in a different ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts to' takes the first letters of prepare and broth, PB, and 'with' sets OTHER between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A leafy plant used in cooking, such as parsley, is a kitchen herb added to soups.

clue.text: Hot-seat involved with rain and wet?

definitions.text: Hot-seat involved with rain and wet?

indicators.note: involved means intricately entangled, so these letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: Someone in a pressured position dealing with rainy, wet conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges HOTSEAT, RAIN and WET together; the whole clue hints at a place recording rain and wet, somewhere a forecaster might feel in the hot seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A facility that measures rainfall, temperature and wind records conditions such as rain and wet.

clue.text: Almost permitted crash on river, checking instrument?

indicators.note: a crash smashes and scrambles the letters
almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

explanation.surface: Someone nearly allowed to have a crash beside a river while checking an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the final D, and 'crash' rearranges what is left as TRIPMETE; 'checking' just introduces the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's resettable odometer measures the distance of a single journey.

clue.text: Wised-up about a fly way to spoil things

indicators.note: the wise word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a sage is wise, someone wised-up
a bot is the larva of the botfly

explanation.surface: Someone clever dealing with a fly in the ointment that ruins things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' looks like an adjective meaning sharp, but it is the insect whose larva is a bot.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberate destruction or obstruction is a method of wrecking plans.

clue.text: Co-operation with international parley arranged

indicators.note: arranged means put into order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Countries cooperating after setting up international talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' gives ERPLAY; 'with' simply joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutual action or reciprocal influence between parties is a kind of working together.

clue.text: Endlessly wander about in shock, given endorsement

indicators.note: the shortened word goes in the word for shock

parts.note: to appal is to shock

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: to rove is to wander about

explanation.surface: Someone aimlessly roaming in a daze, then given official approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' belongs with 'wander' (to rove), while 'Endlessly' drops its final E and 'in' does the containing.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal acceptance or sanction is the same as support or endorsement.

clue.text: Admitting most likely prognosis

annotationWithheld.why: Admitting most likely prognosis (14) gives PREDICTABILITY, but no wordplay in these words builds it and 'most likely prognosis' does not define it; the clue may belong to another light or be misprinted.

clue.text: Sounding drunk, newlywed almost got cross

indicators.note: the word is heard, giving a written form that matches its sound

parts.note: high means intoxicated

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is missing

parts.note: a bride is a woman newly wed

explanation.surface: A tipsy-sounding newlywed nearly turned angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounding' makes HY, said the same as the word for drunk. 'Cross' is a noun here: a cross between breeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A mix of two breeds or varieties is a crossbreed.

clue.text: Soldiers finally going for prescribed treatment

indicators.note: the final letter of the soldiers' word goes away

parts.note: a regiment is a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops eventually setting off for medical treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally going' drops the T from REGIMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed course of diet, exercise or medication.

clue.text: Good smallest pig made it

parts.note: the runt is the smallest of a litter of piglets

explanation.surface: A tiny piglet has done well for itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: the noise a little pig makes is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The low snorting noise of a pig is what a runt piglet would make.

clue.text: Given a directive, incorporating worst-case scenario?

indicators.note: the phrase incorporates, holds within it, a run of letters

explanation.surface: Someone handed instructions that cover the worst outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorporating' finds the letters inside 'Given A DIRective'.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest point, figuratively the worst moment, is what a worst-case scenario represents.

clue.text: Lewis's whimsical description of a flapper one night?

definitions.text: Lewis's whimsical description of a flapper one night?

parts.words: Lewis's whimsical description of a flapper one night?
parts.note: Lewis Carroll's Hatter sings that a bat flies above the world like a household serving board in the sky; a flapper of the night is a bat

explanation.surface: An author's fanciful portrait of a 1920s party girl out for the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis is Lewis Carroll; in Alice the Hatter parodies Twinkle Twinkle: 'Up above the world you fly, like a [this] in the sky.' 'Flapper' suggests a 1920s girl but means a bat.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hatter's simile compares a flying bat to a tray for carrying cups and teapot.

clue.text: Bikini, perhaps, shown to everyone around

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A two-piece swimsuit worn on show for all to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bikini' suggests the swimsuit but is the Pacific nuclear test site; 'shown' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bikini in the Marshall Islands is an example of a ring-shaped coral reef island.

clue.text: Going up the pole?

parts.note: an athlete using a long pole to spring up and over a bar, as in the field event

explanation.surface: Someone climbing a pole, or going a little mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up the pole' is British slang for crazy, steering away from the athletic leap.
explanation.definitionFit: To leap over a bar with the aid of a pole is the athletics jump.

clue.text: One securing Alsatian to take part in pursuit and arrest

parts.note: to dog is to follow in pursuit
to collar a suspect is to arrest them

explanation.surface: A police dog brought along to help chase and catch a suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: A band worn round a pet's neck holds the animal secure, here a German shepherd.

clue.text: Note replacing another in collection of editions of books

indicators.note: one musical note takes the place of a different one in the word

parts.note: a library is a collection of books and editions
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A note swapped out in a list of published editions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing another' puts TE where the note B stood in LIBRARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to written works and authorship, so concerning books.

clue.text: Sadly upset about theatre's closure — hugely entertained there?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, around, the next piece
upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are jumbled
the closure of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A gloomy note about a theatre shutting down after its audiences loved it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges SADLY, and 'about' wraps it round E, the 'closure' of theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian who slayed the audience entertained them enormously, an informal sense of killing.
